speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
role: Acting President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
title: Christ-Centered Unity
summary: President Uchtdorf teaches that baptism makes us both covenant individuals and part of a covenant people, and that Jesus Christ unites people across every worldly boundary while Satan works to divide them. He opens with his great-grandchildren's baptisms and his own baptism in a deep swimming pool, then points to the Nephites and Lamanites, who became one when Christ came, and to the sacrament, where no one is addressed by name. He asks everyone, wherever they are, to start unifying now, to use the sacrament as a weekly fresh start, and to come and see, help, and belong.

President Henry B. Eyring once shared his “hope … that a great day of unity is coming” (“Our Hearts Knit as One,” Liahona, Nov. 2008, 68). It comes in part as we participate in the gathering of Israel, what President Russell M. Nelson called “the greatest challenge, the greatest cause, and the greatest work on earth today” (“Hope of Israel” [worldwide youth devotional, June 3, 2018], Gospel Library).
